reading.body:
CyrusOne Norwalk (NYM5) offers 4 MW of IT capacity across 168,000 square feet, a low power density of about 24 watts per square foot that signals colocation or legacy design rather than dense AI compute.

The 4 MW figure is the total power envelope for servers, while the 168,000 square feet of technical space gives roughly 42 square feet per kilowatt. That ratio leaves most of the building underutilized for high-power AI hardware, which typically concentrates far more electrical load per rack. The data does not include rack-level power or GPU counts, so the 4 MW ceiling alone cannot confirm what compute the site can actually support.

SSAE 16 Type II certification covers audited physical and logical access controls, not power or compute capacity. It makes the facility suitable for regulated colocation workloads, but it does not raise the 4 MW limit. The suitability score of 49, with announced expansion missing, indicates the published data shows no declared path to larger capacity, and it omits connectivity, latency, and rack density metrics that would matter for AI placement.
